mappings.preservedMeaning: The inventory establishes no lifecycle-managed Azure aggregate that contains compute nodes as one infrastructure unit.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: An ARM resource group is outside this inventory, and VM scale sets are compute groups rather than a provider-neutral infrastructure aggregate.

evidence.supports: No inventoried native endpoint represents the proposed aggregate boundary.

mappings.preservedMeaning: A virtual machine scale set is a named, lifecycle-managed collection of virtual-machine instances with capacity semantics.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: The schema does not establish the neutral concept's generic collective load-balancer-backend selection semantics, and Azure scale-set behavior is more specific than an arbitrary compute group.

evidence.supports: The pinned REST schema exposes a PUT lifecycle boundary for a virtual machine scale set.

mappings.preservedMeaning: An Azure virtual machine is a lifecycle-managed information-processing resource provisioned with machine sizing and an execution environment.

evidence.supports: The pinned REST schema exposes the virtual-machine PUT resource boundary.

mappings.preservedMeaning: An Azure virtual network is a managed logical network boundary to which compute interfaces connect.

evidence.supports: The pinned REST schema exposes a virtual-network PUT resource boundary.

mappings.preservedMeaning: The subnet child resource has its own addressable identity inside a virtual network and represents an IP network segment.

evidence.supports: The pinned REST schema exposes a distinct subnet PUT child-resource boundary.

mappings.preservedMeaning: The Azure subnet carries IP prefix and related Layer-3 configuration.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: Azure binds this configuration to an identified subnet child resource; it is not merely composable configuration applied to the same virtual-network resource.

evidence.supports: The schema places address-prefix configuration on the subnet model.

mappings.preservedMeaning: A network interface is an explicit managed connectivity object used by compute and carrying IP configurations that refer to subnets.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: The compute-to-interface reference and interface-to-subnet IP configuration are distributed across resource properties rather than represented by one explicit link resource.

evidence.supports: The pinned REST schema exposes the network-interface PUT resource boundary.

mappings.preservedMeaning: A network security group is a managed, assignable network-security policy object containing traffic-filtering rules.

evidence.supports: The pinned REST schema exposes the network-security-group PUT resource boundary.

mappings.preservedMeaning: An Azure security-rule child resource filters traffic by direction, protocol, ports, prefixes, priority, and action.

evidence.supports: The pinned REST schema exposes a distinct security-rule PUT child-resource boundary.

mappings.preservedMeaning: An SSH public-key resource manages public-key material for virtual-machine access and provisioning.

evidence.supports: The pinned REST schema exposes an SSH-public-key PUT resource boundary.

mappings.preservedMeaning: An Azure compute image is a managed execution-environment image selectable when creating compute.

evidence.supports: The pinned REST schema exposes the managed-image PUT resource boundary.

mappings.preservedMeaning: A virtual machine embeds a vmSize selection that determines compute capacity and machine sizing characteristics.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: The selection is configuration on a VM rather than an independently identified reusable profile, and the schema candidate does not establish portable profile contents or reuse semantics.

evidence.supports: The pinned schema models VM size as embedded hardware-profile configuration on the inventoried virtual-machine resource.

mappings.preservedMeaning: An Azure managed disk is a lifecycle-managed storage resource with capacity that can be attached to compute.

evidence.supports: The pinned REST schema exposes the managed-disk PUT resource boundary.

mappings.preservedMeaning: A virtual machine embeds data-disk entries that associate storage with the compute instance and carry attachment settings.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: The attachment is relationship configuration within the VM storage profile, not an independently identified attachment resource; portable guest-mount semantics are not established.

evidence.supports: The pinned schema places data-disk attachment entries in configuration of the inventoried virtual-machine resource.

mappings.preservedMeaning: A virtual machine embeds customData supplied at creation and made available inside the VM for bootstrap processing.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: The schema says Azure saves the decoded data as a file but does not itself guarantee that the data is executed at the end of boot; execution depends on the guest image and bootstrap mechanism.

evidence.supports: The pinned schema defines base64-encoded custom data on the inventoried VM creation model, saved as a file in the virtual machine and not updatable after creation.

mappings.preservedMeaning: An Azure Load Balancer is a lifecycle-managed network load-balancing resource.

evidence.supports: The pinned REST schema exposes the load-balancer PUT resource boundary.

mappings.preservedMeaning: The inventoried load balancer contains frontend IP configurations and load-balancing rules that together carry listener address, protocol, and port semantics.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: Azure splits the neutral listener across child configurations rather than one listener object; their schema PUT paths are absent from the current inventory, so this containing-resource mapping cannot preserve their distinct child identities.

evidence.supports: The pinned schema exposes a load-balancing-rule PUT path, but its native ID is absent from azure-inventory.json.
The pinned schema separately exposes frontend configuration, confirming composite Azure listener semantics.

mappings.preservedMeaning: A backend address pool is an identified load-balancer child resource grouping selected backend addresses or interfaces.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: Forwarding protocol and frontend/backend ports belong to the load-balancing rule rather than the backend pool, so the pool preserves backend selection but not the full neutral backend-group meaning.

evidence.supports: The pinned REST schema exposes a backend-address-pool PUT child-resource boundary.

mappings.preservedMeaning: The inventoried load balancer contains probes carrying protocol, port, interval, and health-threshold configuration.
mappings.lostOrDifferentMeaning: The probe is a distinct Azure child configuration whose PUT path is absent from the current inventory, so the containing-resource mapping erases probe identity and does not prove runtime necessity.

evidence.supports: The pinned schema exposes a probe PUT child-resource path whose native ID is absent from azure-inventory.json.
